title: What is the PostgreSQL equivalent of Oracle's `CLOB` data type (`TEXT`)?
shortTitle: PostgreSQL Equivalent of Oracle's CLOB Data Type (TEXT)

s1_definition.oneliner: Oracle's `CLOB` maps to PostgreSQL's `TEXT`: a plain, unlimited-length string type you read and write like any normal column.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Oracle CLOB** – a Character Large OBject storing up to about 4 GB, accessed through a LOB locator and `DBMS_LOB` procedures.
- **PostgreSQL TEXT** – a native variable-length character type with no declared length limit (up to about 1 GB per value), used like any ordinary column.
- **Same underlying type** – in PostgreSQL, `VARCHAR(n)`, `VARCHAR`, and `TEXT` are all the same storage; the only difference is the optional length check.
- **TOAST** – PostgreSQL automatically moves large values out-of-line into TOAST storage and compresses them transparently.
- **Migration mapping** – `CLOB` → `TEXT`, `NCLOB` → `TEXT`, `VARCHAR2` → `VARCHAR` or `TEXT`, `BLOB` → `BYTEA`.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India storing a customer's long complaint letter. In Oracle you put it in a special oversized drawer called a CLOB that needs its own handling procedure. In PostgreSQL you use a TEXT column: the same drawer you use for a short name works for a whole book, with no special drawer to manage.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Oracle                          PostgreSQL
  ┌───────────────────┐          ┌───────────────────┐
  │ VARCHAR2(4000)    │    ──▶   │ VARCHAR / TEXT     │
  │ (small strings)   │          │ (no size split)    │
  ├───────────────────┤          │                    │
  │ CLOB              │    ──▶   │ TEXT               │
  │ (up to 4 GB)      │          │ (up to ~1 GB)      │
  │ LOB locator       │          │ Plain column       │
  │ DBMS_LOB API      │          │ Standard SQL       │
  └───────────────────┘          │ TOAST (auto)       │
                                 └───────────────────┘

  Oracle requires the LOB split.
  PostgreSQL unifies everything as TEXT.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The PostgreSQL equivalent of Oracle's CLOB is TEXT. In Oracle, CLOB is a special large-character type holding up to about 4 GB, accessed through a LOB locator and DBMS_LOB procedures. PostgreSQL removes that split: TEXT is a native variable-length string with no declared length and a practical ceiling of about 1 GB, and VARCHAR(n), VARCHAR, and TEXT are all the same underlying type.

You read and write a TEXT column with ordinary SELECT and INSERT, with no locator and no streaming API. PostgreSQL transparently moves large values out-of-line into TOAST storage and compresses them. You can even add a GIN full-text index on a TEXT column, which Oracle CLOB cannot do without Oracle Text.

At the National Bank of India, when migrating the complaints system from Oracle to PostgreSQL, the narratives that had lived in CLOB columns became TEXT, and the locator-based access code collapsed into plain queries. Rajesh also added a GIN full-text index for searching complaints.

Remember one sentence: Oracle CLOB becomes PostgreSQL TEXT, a plain unlimited-length string you treat like any normal column.

---

keyPoints: Oracle CLOB stores up to 4 GB via a LOB locator; PostgreSQL TEXT stores up to about 1 GB as a plain column.
In PostgreSQL, VARCHAR(n), VARCHAR, and TEXT are the same underlying type with identical performance.
TOAST automatically moves large TEXT values out-of-line and compresses them transparently.
Migration mapping: CLOB to TEXT, NCLOB to TEXT, VARCHAR2 to VARCHAR, BLOB to BYTEA.
TEXT columns support full-text search with GIN indexes, which Oracle CLOB cannot do without Oracle Text.
For ordinary large text, always prefer TEXT over PostgreSQL large objects (lo_* functions).
In Java, read and write TEXT with getString/setString like any other string column.
